summary: Today’s pulse tracks Oil price dives as US and Iran pause attacks, Three dead and several injured in shooting at food festival near Seattle's Space Needle, and California man rescued alive after 30 days stranded at sea with broken mast. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are violence, domestic, and family. In the background, Senate to begin voting on Trump intelligence nominee Jay Clayton – US politics live and Secret tape recordings and ‘sham’ payments: the Liberals’ internal ideological war laid bare keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Oil price dives as US and Iran pause attacks
headlines.description: The US says attacks on Iran have been halted to give "talks some space", raising hopes of a resolution to the conflict.

headlines.title: Three dead and several injured in shooting at food festival near Seattle's Space Needle
headlines.description: Police say two suspects were shooting at each other and one of them is in custody and one at large.

headlines.title: California man rescued alive after 30 days stranded at sea with broken mast
headlines.description: Kai Sato used PVC pipes and kayak paddles to try to repair his boat, and a plastic bag to collect condensation to drink A California man was rescued alive drifting in his sailboat off Hawaii after spending 30 days stranded at sea. Kai Sato, 39, set sail from California’s Catalina Islands on 7 June hoping to complete his first solo sail across the Pacific Ocean, he told Hawaii News Now . But his journey took a disastrous turn when his mast snapped, and the phone he was using for navigation died.

Without me, there would be no Israel. .@LeaderJohnThune, I hereby object to any effort to put the Senate into recess in August—at least until such time as the Senate has passed the SAVE America Act—and hereby request a roll call vote. Do not assume you have my consent. You do not.

headlines.title: Secret tape recordings and ‘sham’ payments: the Liberals’ internal ideological war laid bare
headlines.description: The NSW anti-corruption watchdog has begun a public inquiry into allegations of branch stacking, illegal donations, and interference with preselections On Monday, on the first day of the corruption watchdog’s inquiry into operation Rosny, an investigation into allegations of “possible offences under the Electoral Funding Act”, we heard boasts on secret tape recordings from a developer that he had “my hands on the state government” and he had “fucked” the career of a state politician by “taking his seat”. As for the state’s building commissioner, David Chandler, who was a thorn in the developer’s side, he was going to “fuck him sideways”.

headlines.title: Pauline Hanson and Malcolm Roberts deride family law system, calling DV a ‘weapon’ and court a ‘slaughterhouse’
headlines.description: Exclusive: Resurfaced comments by the One Nation leader underline her criticism of paid family violence leave and domestic violence support groups Pauline Hanson told a podcast last year she believed “your employer should not be responsible” for providing paid domestic violence leave, while her colleague Malcolm Roberts recently referred to the family court as the “slaughterhouse of the nation”, in the latest One Nation comments critical of the family law system to emerge. Hanson claimed on a 2021 podcast that domestic violence was being “used as a weapon” in court proceedings, and criticised domestic violence groups for focusing on support for women.

headlinePool.description: Mayo finally ended a 75-year wait for the county's fourth All-Ireland Senior Football title on Sunday.

headlinePool.title: Poll shows Labour ahead of Reform UK for first time since Burnham became PM – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: The Green party has its lowest share of the vote since Zack Polanski became leader, data shows I have already posted lines from Andy Burnham ’s BBC interview on reforming social care (see 9.03am ), making council tax fairer (see 10.03am ), and ruling out an early election (see 11.56am ). And yesterday Peter Walker wrote up the lines in the interview from Burnham saying he would disagree with Donald Trump if necessary. Here are some of the other comments worth flagging up. Burnham suggested care workers should be exempt from Shabana Mahmood’s plan to make foreign workers wait much longer until they can apply for indefinite leave to remain in the UK. Currently workers normally have to wait five years until they qualify for settlement. Under Mahmood’s plans, the norm will become 10 years, and care workers could even have to wait 15 years (because working in a low-pay sector means they contribute less to the exchequer, the Home Office argues ). Last week Kiran Stacey and Patrick Butler reported that Burnham may order a rethink.

headlinePool.title: ‘I knew what he had done to those boys’: murderer to stay in jail after journalist’s fight for justice
headlinePool.description: Gibraltar-based Ros Astengo inspired four men to report sexual assaults carried out by Allan Grimson in 1990s Ros Astengo, a journalist based in Gibraltar who usually focuses on politics and social issues, had qualms when she began investigating the case of the suspected serial killer Allan Grimson as he neared release from prison after serving more than 20 years. She worried that she might reopen the scars of survivors of Grimson – but also that she could be putting herself in the “crosshairs” of a dangerous man who had sexually assaulted and battered two young men to death in the late 1990s when he was a Royal Navy petty officer.

headlinePool.title: ‘You say genocide, I say war’: Boy George releases pro-Israel song, We Will Dance Again
headlinePool.description: Culture Club singer sings ‘I stand with the Jews / I don’t feel brave, I just need to behave like a human’, in song defending Israel’s response to Hamas attack Boy George has released a new song entitled We Will Dance Again, which voices support for Israel’s military action in Palestine. Posted on X and Instagram with the Hebrew title עוד נרקוד alongside its English translation, the song features a pop-reggae backing. The opening lyrics are: “You say genocide, I say war / When you’re attacked, that’s what the army’s for / Does it get ugly? You bet it does / When I know you wanna kill every last one of us.”

headlinePool.title: Off-duty police officer detains man who attacked three women with knives in Paris
headlinePool.description: Women aged 19, 24 and 36 taken to hospital after assault in Porte de Clichy area in north of capital A French off-duty police officer has detained a man after he attacked and wounded three women with two kitchen knives in Paris on Monday. Three women aged 19, 24 and 36 were taken to hospital after the assault at about 11.30am (0930 GMT) in the Porte de Clichy area in the north of the capital, said the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez.

headlinePool.title: Devastating European wildfires in maps - and how they're being tackled
headlinePool.description: A blaze near Bordeaux has torn through more than 162 sq miles (420 sq km) in less than four days, while the Madrid region is seeing its worst fires ever.

headlinePool.title: Oil price slides as US and Iran pause fire; cancer treatments help AstraZeneca beat profit forecasts – as it happened
headlinePool.description: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news The UK’s financial watchdog has launched a £2m advertising campaign aimed at curbing use of claims management companies (CMCs), and encouraging drivers hit by the car finance scandal to file their own complaints. The Financial Conduct Authority’s 30-second video advert features a series of pedestrians jumping over car bonnets in slow-motion, action film style, while text flashes across the screen to encourage their peers to “Feel Claim Confident.” Many people who may be owed compensation aren’t sure where to start or don’t realise they don’t have to pay someone to make a complaint. Our free tools are there to help people feel claim confident – so they can get any money owed back without it costing them a penny.”

headlinePool.title: First Kenyan to play in NFL deported under Trump immigration crackdown
headlinePool.description: Former rugby star Daniel Adongo allegedly overstayed visa but supporters say he needed mental health help A former rugby star who became the first Kenyan to play in the NFL , was deported in June for a visa overstay and multiple arrests, according to federal immigration authorities. Daniel Adongo, 37, spent two seasons as a linebacker for the Indianapolis Colts, playing twice, and was cut in 2015 after facing domestic violence allegations. His visa expired in 2016, but he remained in the US, a press statement from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.

headlinePool.title: Father and daughter die after being pulled from sea at Cornish beach
headlinePool.description: Police appeal for help to find handbag woman was carrying when she entered the water at Fistral beach in Newquay A father and daughter have died after being pulled from the sea at a popular surfing beach in the Cornish resort of Newquay. The man, in his 60s, and the woman, in her 30s, were pronounced dead at Fistral beach on Sunday after a large emergency response involving coastguards, a rescue helicopter, an RNLI lifeboat, paramedics and police. The pair were from Doncaster, South Yorkshire.
